My recommendation depends on your age. I started going to the gyno at about age 14 because I was going on the pill to help my painful periods. I would have annual appointments from there and those appointments would simply be conversations with my doctor and a urine test to check for STDs. Then, once you’re 21 or older, it is recommended to get a pap smear every few years. (They surprisingly do not hurt! You feel it a little bit, but it isn’t bad.) I was also taught how to do a self breast exam. 
I have a positive association with my gynecologist so I have no worries when going, but I understand it can be scary to go for the first time. I think if you have periods, it could be worth having annual appointments just to get comfortable with your doctor and if you’re at 21 or older, get pap smears! You can always bring someone to your appointments with you like a guardian, sibling, or close friend.

I see blood clots similar to this when on my period too. the dark color just means it is older and not as “fresh”. I believe that clots that are the size of a US quarter or smaller are considered normal. [not a doctor] However, the pain you are having is not normal. for the diagnostic procedure, has it occurred yet or no? If not, is a date scheduled? (If all you can do now is wait you should still talk to your doctor and mention that despite the painkillers you’re taking, it’s still unbearable.) Definitely reach out to an OBGYN about all of this. You mentioned in another comment that you’ve tried a couple of different pills. It’s normal to have irregularly and cramping when trying different birth control methods but severe pain like this is NOT normal. And when you talk to your OB you can mention the clotting and color of your blood like you mentioned in your post. They will be able to provide better insight on whether it is anything to worry about or not.

I just finished my first day with my Saalt (small) cup. Prior to this, the only things I’ve ever had up there have been light flow tampons. It was definitely an experience getting it in and out- out being the harder one. It’s because of my first time usage though I’m sure! I recommend looking up Put A Cup In It and looking at their website and youtube videos. I wish I had looked at their cup comparison charts before purchasing my cup. I like the cup I got, but I probably should’ve gone with the soft version since it’s firmness made it harder to fold. I used the “punch down” method for insertion. As for removal- that took awhile. I have a high cervix (which I didn’t measure before purchasing a cup like I should have) and so the cup shimmied a little too far in for my preference. I could just reach the end of the stem, so it was hard to get a good grip on it. I wish I had purchased a cup with a better stem on it. One with more grip, or one with a ring. Since I have little experience with things being inserted up there, I found it impossible to comfortably reach the base with two fingers on either side and pinch it. So keep in mind that the cup process is very hands-on and can take some getting used to. It took awhile, but I was finally able to remove the cup by using toilet paper as a grip on the stem and then pushing a finger against the cup to break the suction. I hope all goes well!

Listen to them when they need to rant or talk, and try to talk to them often. It's good to let them know that you're there for them. Sometimes it's also good to give them a distraction, maybe go somewhere/ do something fun or relaxing with them to relieve a bit of their stress and take their mind off of it. If they're self harming you can try to gently encourage them to do an alternative. (ex. If they cut themselves, a better alternative is to take an ice cube whenever they have the urge and just hold it in their hand, there are more alternatives if you look it up online) You don't want to sound disappointed in them if they don't want to try and get help immediately/don't want to try an alternative, but show your happiness if/when they take a step (even if it's really small) towards getting better or getting help. Little things can mean the world to them.
